voyage-latino.title: Latin journey
voyage-latino.description: Beyond cumbia: more ways to make a ukulele groove.

reggaeton-01-dembow.title: Reggaeton: strumming with the snare
reggaeton-01-dembow.description: Here the grid is in 16th notes (16 steps). You strum exactly together with the dembow snare: 3 + 3 + 2. Chords: the "vi – IV – I – V" progression from a thousand hits.
reggaeton-01-dembow.goal: Stay glued to the snare, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Find the snare lane in "The band": those are your strums.
Count "1 e & a, 2 e & a…": your strums land on the "a" of 1 and the & of 2, then the same on 3 and 4.
Start by muting every track except kick and snare.

son-01-clave.title: Son cubano: playing with the clave
son-01-clave.description: The clave (wooden claves, a high "tock" sound) plays a 2-bar pattern the whole orchestra follows. You keep a steady pattern with a chuck on 2 and 4: listen to how your playing and the clave lock together.
son-01-clave.goal: Don't let the clave throw you off, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: First mute everything except the clave and listen to it for 4 loops while counting: "1 . . 2-& . 4 | . 2 3 .".
The bass plays "ahead" (on the & of 2 and on 4): don't follow it, follow the click.
I – IV – V chords: C, F, G7. The F only takes two fingers.

bossa-01-pouce-doigts.title: Bossa nova: thumb and fingers
bossa-01-pouce-doigts.description: No strumming here: your thumb (P) plucks the C string on beats 1 and 3 like a bass, and your fingers (F) pinch the C-E-A strings together, offset. The chords are easy (Am7 = all open strings!) so you can focus on coordination.
bossa-01-pouce-doigts.goal: Steady thumb, offset fingers, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: First practice the thumb alone on 1 and 3, then add the fingers.
The finger pattern is similar to the "rim" in the band: listen to it.

chachacha-01-4-et-1.title: Cha-cha-chá: the "4-&-1"
chachacha-01-4-et-1.description: All of cha-cha-chá fits into three strums: the 4, the & of 4, and the next 1. That's the "cha-cha-chá" the dancers call out. Here you play the beats, and add that little upstroke just before the 1.
tips: Say "1, 2, 3, cha-cha": the "cha-cha" lands on 4-&, then the 1 comes back.
Listen to the güiro: its two short little scrapes are exactly your "4-&".
Don't rush the &: it sits right in the middle, like the other off-beats.

chachacha-02-mineur.title: Minor cha-cha-chá with a chuck
chachacha-02-mineur.description: Let's build on it: a chuck on 2 (like an orchestra's snare drum), then the "cha-cha-chá" on 4-&-1. With a progression in A minor, very typical of orchestral cha-cha-chás.
chachacha-02-mineur.goal: Pattern and changes with no gaps, 2 loops at 105 bpm.
tips: The pattern: down, chuck, down, down-up. Practice it on Am alone before starting the progression.
Use the chuck on 2 to relax your right hand.
Dm → E7 is still the tricky change: get ready for it from beat 3 of the Dm bar.
